Privacy

This notice is a plain-language summary for Veylet Studio (Australia). Last updated 25 September 2026. It is not legal advice.

What we collect. Your email address, which is how you sign in and how we reach you. The captures you send us, and the walkthroughs made from them. Your plan’s purchase state from the App Store — whether a subscription is active, which product it is, and when it renews — never your card number, your Apple ID or your payment details, which Apple keeps and we never see. And counts of use: walkthroughs sent, accepted, handoffs created and revoked, so the plan’s allowance can be counted and your desk can show it. We do not build a profile of you, and we ask for no more than the work needs.

What we never do. We never sell, rent or trade personal information, and we run no advertising cookies and no third-party trackers. Your captures are not used to advertise to you and are not passed to anyone outside Veylet without your instruction.

Enquiries. Apply and request forms go to yoda@yodalai.xyz via FormSubmit. Use them to assess a walkthrough or operator application. Do not send access codes, identity documents or private client images.

Accounts. Account access is currently a limited studio test; contact the studio before your first sign-in. When access is available, signing in with an email address either returns you to an account that already exists for that address or creates one — there is no separate sign-up step, and the first sign-in is the account being made. It is a hosted identity so the same person can use the website and the iPhone app. Identity and related records are stored with Supabase in Sydney (ap-southeast-2). Sign-in is not operator approval and is not payment. We never merge two accounts that share an email address.

Your records. Spaces you save hold a name, a category and a suburb or city. They must not hold a street address, unit number, access code, identity document or private client image, and the desk rejects an address-shaped location. You can download a file of your spaces and tours from your desk at any time, and ask us to correct anything that is wrong.

Room captures on your device. Veylet Capture saves camera photographs, LiDAR depth and camera-position data locally so you can inspect and export a capture. The current beta does not automatically upload original room captures to Veylet. When you export through the device's share menu, the package goes to the app or recipient you choose. Device backups and third-party sharing services follow your settings with those services.

Tour files. When you send a reconstructed tour from Veylet Capture, the package is stored privately for the property's workspace. Active workspace members can open finished tours for review. Unfinished uploads remain available only to their uploader while that membership is active. A client handoff lets anyone holding its link open the shared tour. Street addresses, access codes and ID documents do not belong in these records.

How walkthroughs are processed. Walkthroughs are processed automatically on cloud GPUs in Australia (Modal, Sydney region). No Veylet staff member views a capture as part of normal processing. An automatic quality check decides whether a walkthrough is ready for your review. An AI visual check is planned; it will be listed here before it is switched on.

Client handoff links. A handoff is an unlisted link you choose to create for one tour. Anyone holding that link can open the walkthrough; it asks the client for no account, and Revoke stops it working. Handoff and preview pages are excluded from search engines. Do not pass a link to anyone who should not see the space.

Deleting your account. Ask in the app or on your desk at veylet.com/account. We complete the deletion within 30 days and confirm when it is done. You cannot undo it yourself. When it completes, your account, its spaces and its walkthroughs are removed, every handoff link and embed stops working, and hosting of every released walkthrough ends with them — deletion ends hosting at once, without the 14 days that follow the end of a plan. Remove the links and embeds from your listing too, because copies people already downloaded cannot be recalled.

What deletion covers. Hosted capture files, generated walkthroughs and the account records used to deliver them are removed. Once removal starts, these files cannot be restored through your account. Copies on your own device, exported files and copies already downloaded by someone else are outside this account deletion. Contact us about any copies held separately by the studio.

Limited records we retain. Invoices, receipts and minimal records of payments, accepted services and deletion may be retained for accounting and legal obligations. These retained records do not provide access to your imagery, captures or walkthroughs. Deleting a Veylet account does not cancel a subscription billed by Apple; manage that subscription in your Apple account.

Cloudflare provides hosting and website performance measurements. Hosting logs may also exist at Vercel and Supabase. An App Store subscription is sold and charged by Apple; this public site does not collect card numbers.

Ask to access, correct or delete your account data: yoda@yodalai.xyz. We keep enquiry mail as needed to assess a job, then no longer than the work requires. If you are not satisfied with how we handled a privacy question, you can complain to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

Veylet Studio is operated by Yo-Da Lai, a sole trader (ABN 84 992 526 369) in south-east Queensland, Australia, who is responsible for the personal information described here.
